title: An English royalist letter in a numerical code, September 1645 (TNA SP 106/10 f. 251, DECODE R931)

transcription.notes: DECODE transcription by FK (2020) checked against the image; ~192 numbers 10-260 with clear words

system.summary: A numerical code of numbers 10-260 separated by dots, with clear English words between them; about 104 distinct numbers in about 192: a nomenclator, not a letter cipher.
system.notes: Split 14 Oct 2026 from sp106box10; not part of the 1623-25 file.

conditions.human_role: nothing beyond setting the target; images fetched with the project DECODE cookie

solution.what: Catalogue 58: fetched DECODE metadata and images for R656, R662, R722, R931 and neighbours (R655, R657, R663, R930, R932); R931 and R932 carry DECODE transcriptions, R932 also Lasry's key.
R931 (Sept 1645, 104 distinct numbers in 192): applied Lasry's TNA SP 106, SP106-2, SP106-5, SP106-8 keys and the R932 Goring key.

R931: compared with Charles I to Culpeper 1645 key (BL Add MS 32256 ff. 6-7, DECODE R9117/R9118): words 300-600, nothing in 100-260; does not fit. R9116 (Charles I to the Queen, Oxford 1642) is only a frequency tally with no values and R9119 f. 8 a blank ruled sheet.
Entry split from sp106box10 under the one-key rule (Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): R931 is a 1645 royalist letter, not part of the 1623-25 file. DECODE transcription copied to the folder. No new attack.

outcome.method_basis: George Lasry's 1645-46 SP 106 keys (TNA SP 106, SP106-2, -3, -5, -8) and the Charles I to Culpeper 1645 key (R9117/R9118) were applied and none fits (coverage at most 0.45, gibberish).
outcome.notes: Split on 14 Oct 2026 from sp106box10; catalogue 58 stays open for it.
outcome.fraction_read_source: R931_decode_transcription.txt: no number has a value

gaps.detail: none of the known 1645 royalist keys fits; the matching key (Digby / Nicholas / Goring, BL Add MS 32256 ff. 4-9, Egerton 2550) not found
